deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 172r of R.AbelTheta. The previous page deals with Abel's theorem, Jacobi inversion and the congruence Σ_μ u_π(ε_μ) ≡ (b_1,…,b_p) for the level sets of a rational function ρ. The next page builds explicit theta quotients θ(v − gπi − Σh a)/θ(v)·e^{−2Σ h v}. This page states and starts proving when an algebraic function of z can be written as a quotient of two products of equally many theta functions. It is draft material for Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen (1857), Part II, on representing algebraic functions by theta quotients.

(1) Heading. 'We now investigate which algebraic functions of z can be represented as quotients of two products of ϑ-functions.'

(2) Necessary condition. Write the expression as Φ = Π_k ϑ(u − e_k) / Π_k ϑ(u − e'_k), with the same number of factors above and below (cf. next page). Use the quasi-periodicity ϑ(v + πi e_μ) = ϑ(v) and ϑ(v + a_μ) = exp(−a_{μμ} − 2v_μ) ϑ(v). When the point (s,z) runs round a closed path and returns, every argument shifts by the same period. The exponential factors from numerator and denominator therefore leave a constant multiplier c, independent of (s,z); the terms linear in v cancel because the factor counts are equal. This is my filling, in modern form. Repeating the path n times gives c^n. If Φ is algebraic in z it takes only finitely many values over each z. So the powers c^n form a finite set, which forces c to be a root of unity. Riemann writes this argument twice, the second version cleaner. In the final version the multipliers are attached to crossings of the canonical cuts (Querschnitte) a_ν, b_ν: they must be roots of unity if Φ, continued arbitrarily far, is to have only finitely many values for each z.

(3) Claimed converse (stated, proof deferred with 'Es lässt sich nun leicht zeigen …'). Every algebraic function of z that is single-valued and continuous on the cut surface T' and picks up constant factors across the cuts can be expressed 'auf unzweideutige Art' as a quotient of two products of ϑ-functions. 'Unzweideutig' should be read as unique up to a constant factor and the choice of products.

(4) Abel-type relation for such a multiplicative function ε.
- Let α_μ be the value of u_μ (the normalized integrals of the first kind) at the simple poles of ε, and β_μ its value at the simple zeros. Strictly these are vectors, one sum per u_μ.
- Make log ε single-valued on T': join each simple pole to a simple zero by a line through the interior of T'. Across each line log ε jumps by 2πi, larger on the positive side than on the negative side.
- Integrate log ε·du_μ around the whole boundary of the further-cut surface; the integral is zero.
- The boundary pieces along the connecting lines give 2πi(Σβ − Σα), up to sign.
- The pieces along a_ν, b_ν give the jumps of log ε (2πi g_ν, 2πi h_ν) times the periods of u_μ (πi δ_{μν}, a_{μν}).
- Result, in Riemann's normalization and up to sign conventions (my completion; the formula on the page is unfinished): Σ_k β^{(k)}_μ − Σ_k α^{(k)}_μ = g_μ πi + Σ_ν h_ν a_{μ,ν}.
- For single-valued ε, g_ν and h_ν are integers ('ganze Zahlen'), which is Abel's theorem. For ε with multipliers e^{2πi g_ν}, e^{2πi h_ν}, the g, h are real, and rational when the multipliers are roots of unity.

(5) Final lines, read as a converse. If the zeros and poles are given, the numbers g_ν, h_ν are in general determined by them. Conversely, the points can be chosen so that the factors e^{g_ν 2πi}, e^{h_ν 2πi} take prescribed values. This is the existence of a multiplicative function with given character. The next page realizes it explicitly by the theta quotient whose multipliers are e^{2gπi} and e^{−2hπi}.
errors: No mathematical error in what is actually asserted, but much is incomplete or crossed out. The decisive formula Σβ_μ − Σα_μ = … is left blank on the page; the right-hand side given in the reconstruction is my completion. Signs (e.g. ±g, ±h) depend on orientation conventions that cannot be read off the page.

'Jede algebraische Function … auf unzweideutige Art' is too strong as written. The representation is unique only up to a constant factor and the choice of the theta products. It also applies only to functions that are single-valued on T' with constant multipliers (abelian unramified-type multiplicative functions), not to arbitrary algebraic functions of z. Riemann's hypotheses in the text do impose this restriction.

The root-of-unity argument silently assumes the multiplier c is independent of the starting point. This holds because the same period shifts all theta arguments and the factor counts are equal, but it is not stated on this page.
Writing α_μ, β_μ as single numbers hides that they are sums over all poles and zeros (index k). The sums Σα_μ, Σβ_μ on the page are presumably over these points.

results.what: A quotient of equal-length products of theta functions on a Riemann surface has constant multipliers along closed paths; it is algebraic only if these multipliers are roots of unity.
results.modern_name: Multiplicative (Prym-type) functions with finite-order characters; theta quotients as sections with flat unitary characters
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen (1857), §§ on representing algebraic functions by theta quotients; developed further by Prym (1860s) and Weber

results.what: Relation Σ u(zeros) − Σ u(poles) = gπi + Σ h a for a multiplicative function, obtained by integrating log ε du along the boundary of the cut surface with lines joining poles to zeros.
results.modern_name: Abel's theorem (generalized to multiplicative functions; Abel–Jacobi map and characters / Picard variety)
results.usually_credited_to: Abel (1826/1829) for the theorem; this proof by boundary integration of log ε du is Riemann's (1857)

results.what: Converse: given multipliers, the divisor can be chosen so that the function has those multipliers, realized by θ(v−gπi−Σh a)/θ(v)·e^{−2Σhv} (next page).
results.modern_name: Existence of multiplicative functions with prescribed character; flat line bundles ↔ points of the Jacobian

The same f gains multiplier e^{−2hπi} under v→v+πi (the theta factors are πi-periodic). Should be 0.
An algebraic function has finitely many branches, so its multiplier c satisfies c^n = 1, i.e. c is a root of unity (here the 6th roots).
Genus-1 analogue: θ1(z−b)/θ1(z−a) has multiplier e^{2i(b−a)} under z→z+πτ, since θ1(z+πτ) = −q^{−1}e^{−2iz}θ1(z). It is a root of unity iff b−a ∈ π·Q (mod π), the elliptic form of Σβ−Σα = gπi + h·a.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the insertion above 'Functionen' reads 'von z', and the struck word after it is illegible. Read 'welche algebraische Functionen von z als Quotienten zweier Producte von ϑ Functionen dargestellt werden können'.

'Es sei ε_μ ein Werth von ε … Man bezeichne nun den Werth von ε_μ' should almost certainly read 'u_μ' (the normalized integral). Read 'Man bezeichne nun den Werth von u_μ für ε = ∞ durch α_μ und für ε = 0 durch β_μ'.

The passage about the connecting lines should read roughly: '… nehme log ε, indem man jeden der Punkte, wo ε unendlich von der ersten Ordnung wird, mit je einem Punkte, wo ε unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung wird, durch eine Linie durch das Innere von T' verbindet, längs welcher log ε auf der positiven Seite um 2πi grösser ist als auf der negativen'.
'durch Betrachtung der Begrenzung des Integrals' is better read 'durch Betrachtung der Begrenzung [des Integrals ∫ log ε du_μ]'.
The final line reads 'so bestimmen, dass die Factoren e^{g_ν 2πi}, e^{h_ν 2πi} gegebene Werthe annehmen'. Here g_ν, h_ν are the cut constants, called 'ganze Zahlen' for single-valued ε.
